title: parseDiarizedTranscript's implausible-speaker-label guard used a strict `>` against MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEAKER_LABEL_LENGTH (60), so a garbled speaker capture of EXACTLY 60 chars slipped through as a real speakerRef instead of being recovered as text
evidence: packages/ai/src/stt/gemini-file-upload.ts:151 (pre-fix) `if (speakerRef.length > MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEAKER_LABEL_LENGTH)`. Found live in data/toc-migrated/2026-09-16-pathways-in-psychology/turns.json turn t280: speakerRef was the 60-character string "through any of the three intakes in a year. [32:41] Anuradha" (a mis-split sentence fragment, not a real speaker name) because length===60 is not >60. Repro: node --import tsx -e with the exact 60-char string reproduces the bug against the pre-fix guard.
reproduction: node --import tsx -e "import('./packages/ai/src/stt/gemini-file-upload.ts').then(({parseDiarizedTranscript})=>{const g='through any of the three intakes in a year. [32:41] Anuradha';console.log(g.length);console.log(JSON.stringify(parseDiarizedTranscript('[00:00] Anuradha: intro. [00:05] '+g+': Psychology would only have one intake.')))})"
fix_direction: Change the guard to `>=` so the boundary itself counts as implausible (a real speaker label is never anywhere near 60 chars). Also manually repair any already-written turns.json rows this bug produced.
found_by: maker (u1-toc-sept-catchup, during a routine quality spot-check of freshly transcribed session data)
